question: Should I wear a mask outside in Singapore today?
name: Claude
answer:
It depends on how long you'll be outside and whether you're in a higher-risk group. Singapore is in a serious haze episode, but official advice says most people on a short trip outside don't need an N95.

**Latest air quality (17 Oct, 7am):** The 24-hour PSI is unhealthy across Singapore, highest 191 in Central. The 1-hour PM2.5 is elevated in East, Central, West, North and South — highest 119 µg/m³ in East. That's a bit better than yesterday, when the east, west and central regions recorded "very unhealthy" PSI levels alongside "high" PM2.5 readings. This is Singapore's longest continuous stretch of poor air quality since the 2015 haze crisis.

**What the official advice means for you:**

- **Short trips outside (like commuting):** The Ministry of Health says people generally do not need N95 masks when commuting to work or school, or while indoors.
- **Several hours outside:** If you'll spend several hours outdoors when PM2.5 levels are high or very high, the ministry says you may consider a well-fitted N95 mask or equivalent. Healthy adults should avoid long or strenuous physical activity outdoors.
- **Older people, pregnant women, children, and people with heart or lung conditions:** These groups should cut down on time outside. They may wear an N95 when the forecast is Very Unhealthy (PSI >200) if they have to be outdoors for several hours. Anyone who has difficulty breathing at rest or on exertion should consult their doctor before using an N95 mask.

**Two practical tips:**
- Surgical and cloth masks don't filter out fine haze particles well. If you wear a mask for the haze, use a properly fitted N95.
- If you're in a higher-risk group, you may be able to get free masks. Free N95 masks are being given out through PA Community Clubs and haze mask vending machines at selected public transport hubs, Social Services Offices and PA venues. You can check eligibility on HazeMaskGoWhere.

**In short:** You probably don't need a mask for a quick errand or commute, especially if you're healthy. Wear an N95 if you'll be out for hours, have a health condition, or feel irritation. Readings change every hour, so check haze.gov.sg or the myENV app before you go out. The 1-hour PM2.5 number is the best guide for what the air is like right now.

# Singapore postpones Purple Parade to first half of 2027 amid haze concerns
Over 15,000 people turned up for the biggest edition of The Purple Parade in 2025. - ST

SINGAPORE: The Purple Parade has been postponed amid worsening haze conditions, organisers announced on Thursday (Oct 15).

The event, a ground-up movement that promotes awareness of the special needs community, was set to be held on Oct 24 at Suntec City.

Singapore has been experiencing its longest continuous stretch of poor air quality since the 2015 haze crisis.

Hazy conditions across the island worsened on Oct 16 with the east, west and central regions recording “very unhealthy” Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) levels alongside “high” PM2.5 readings.



At 3pm, the one-hour PM2.5 readings – measured in micrograms per cubic metre and used as a gauge for current air quality – were in the “high” band for two regions: central (182) and west (156).

The north, east and south registered “elevated” readings of 150, 140 and 109 respectively.

The highest PM2.5 reading this haze season was recorded at 3pm on Oct 14 in the western part of the island at 288.

Meanwhile, the 24-hour PSI in the central region at 3pm stood at 229, hitting a new high for this haze season. That lies in the “very unhealthy” range, alongside the east and west regions both measuring 205.

The southern and northern parts of Singapore recorded PSI readings in the “unhealthy” band at that time, measuring 185 and 157 respectively.

Air quality is considered unhealthy when the PSI – a 24-hour rolling average of six key air pollutants – is in the range of 101 to 200 and very unhealthy when it is in the range of 201 to 300.

SINGAPORE, Sept 15 — The current hazy condition persists in Singapore, with the air quality continuing to stay at an unhealthy level.

The National Environment Agency (NEA) said today, the prevailing winds are forecast to blow from the southwest, and the current hazy conditions are expected to persist.

As of 8am today, the 24-hour pollutant standard index (PSI) stood at 122 - 150, and the three-hour PSI at 114.

A 24-hour PSI reading of above 100 indicates unhealthy air quality.

The haze situation could further deteriorate should the current unfavourable winds blow in denser haze from Sumatra.

Thundery showers are forecast for Singapore in early morning hours, but this may only bring a brief temporary respite to the hazy conditions. — Bernama

SINGAPORE, Sept 27 — Air quality has been gradually deteriorating throughout the day, with the 3-hour PSI mark breaching the 100 mark at 2pm today.

As at 6pm, the 24-hour PSI was still in the moderate range at 82-92, while the three-hour PSI was at 145. 
The National Environment Agency (NEA) said in a 5pm update today that the 24-hour PSI over the next 24 hours is expected to be in the low to mid-sections of the unhealthy range, with a possibility of entering the high-section of the Unhealthy range if denser haze is blown in by unfavourable winds. 
Moderate to dense haze is still persisting in central and southern Sumatra, and some haze has spread to the sea areas west and south of Singapore, said the NEA.

The NEA advised healthy persons to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion.
